title: install-smoke-harness-checkpoints-and-observed-failures
text:
Purpose:
This is a working draft of a lightweight smoke-harness and failure-fingerprint reference for VPC/on-prem private deliveries. Focus is on small, fast probes we run pre- and post-terraform changes and during runtime upgrades. The goal is: fail fast, gather consistent signals, and pick the least-surprising rollback when an upgrade goes sideways.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to typical private deployments we ship: single-tenant VPCs and air-gapped on-prem clusters using our terraform modules and the managed runtime container images.
- Assumes operator has: kubectl/ssh access to control plane nodes, terraform creds to state backend, and access to customer logs collection (or instructions to get them).
- Not a full runbook for complex incidents; this is a quick checklist + symptom mapping to accelerate first responders.

Quick smoke-harness (5 stages, ~8-20 minutes total depending on environment):
A) Infra sanity (2-5m)
  - terraform show/plan sanity: terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -refresh=false | tee tf-plan.txt (quickly eyeball for unexpected resource deletes).
  - remote state reachable? terraform state pull > /tmp/state.json; if timeout -> network/credentials problem.
  - verify control-plane VM connectivity: ping/load SSH to primary control node. Check for firewall rules blocking egress to our artifact registry.

B) Node and driver checks (2-4m)
  - ssh to a GPU node: sudo systemctl status nvidia-persistenced || sudo systemctl status nvidia-driver
  - nvidia-smi (must return < 5s) and shows GPUs not in iored state. If hangs, suspect driver/kernel mismatch or hung NVML.
  - dmesg | tail -n 200 for OOM kills, GPU driver reinitialization, or PCI errors.

C) Container runtime and images (2-4m)
  - crictl ps / docker ps: verify runtime healthy. If containerd errors: journalctl -u containerd -n 200.
  - Pull image test: ctr images pull <runtime-image> or docker pull <image>. Timeouts indicate registry egress/credentials issue.

D) Serving runtime basic flow (2-5m)
  - curl local health endpoint: http://localhost:8080/health (or kube port-forward to service). Expect 200 + short JSON.
  - Run a minimal generation request with tiny prompt and short max_tokens to validate KV cache path and tokenizer.

E) End-to-end smoke (2-5m)
  - Run the real smoke script (see commands below) that: sends 3 requests of varying seq lengths and ensures latency within SLO and no kernel-level segfaults.

Quick commands (paste-ready snippets):
- terraform plan quick: TF_IN_AUTOMATION=1 terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars -out=tfplan.binary
- state pull: terraform state pull | jq .resources[]?.type | head -n 30
- kube basic health: kubectl get pods -n redwood -o wide
- pod logs last 200 lines: kubectl logs -n redwood <pod> --tail=200
- nvml probe: ssh node-1 "nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,driver_version,memory.total --format=csv,noheader"

Terraform module sanity checks (notes to self / common gotchas):
- Provider lockfiles: mismatched provider versions between CI planning and operator machine cause plan diffs that bite during apply. Pin provider versions in module root.
- Remote state drift: sometimes onprem teams run manual changes (system updates) that terraform no longer tracks; add a local drift-checker script that compares cloud-init tags (instance IDs) against tfstate.
- Module input validation: we have permissive defaults that hide subtle changes (e.g., default machine_type changed upstream). Add explicit validation step: terraform validate -var-file=prod.tfvars.
- Sensitive outputs: don't push KMS keys into logs. Use lookup scripts instead.

Upgrade plan checklist (preflight → canary → ramp → cutoff):
Preflight (24–48 hours before):
  - Reservation of rollback window with customer and SRE on-call.
  - Confirm canary pool size (1-2 nodes) & backup of tfstate.
  - Snapshot GPU hosts (if supported) or ensure VM image is rebuildable.
  - Run smoke-harness A−E against current stable cluster and store baseline metrics (latency, token/sec).

Canary apply (small subset):
  - Apply terraform changes to canary workspace.
  - Run end-to-end harness 30-min cadence for 3 hours; compare to baseline.
  - Automated checks: token SLO, error rate < 0.5%, GPU OOMs = 0.

Ramp criteria and cutoff:
  - Pass 3 consecutive hours of canary checks -> ramp to 25%.
  - If any regression detected (higher error rate, repeated kernel restarts, failed image pulls), immediate rollback of applied tf changes and restore configurations.

Rollback decision heuristics (simple):
  - Immediate rollback if: control-plane pods crashloop, driver reboots observed, or >5% increased 95th latency across synthetic traffic in 30m.
  - Manual investigation for: intermittent Pod I/O timeouts, transient crictl errors, or failed certificate rotations (may be fixed without full rollback).

Observed failure fingerprints (symptom → quick hypothesis → first probes → short mitigation):
1) Symptom: nvidia-smi hangs or returns NVML error.
   - Hypothesis: driver/kernel mismatch or NVML stuck; possible recent kernel update.
   - Probes: uname -r; rpm -qa | grep -i nvidia; check journalctl -k and dmesg for GPU resets.
   - Mitigation: reboot node (if safe), drain and cordon, or switch to node with older kernel. If frequent, pin kernel-driver combo in config.

2) Symptom: pod fails with SIGSEGV in serving-runtime binary shortly after starting.
   - Hypothesis: incompatible libcuda/GLIBC or mismatched runtime image built on different base.
   - Probes: kubectl describe pod; kubectl logs; check image digest vs expected manifest GH: infra-private#482; check ldd on binary inside debug container.
   - Mitigation: revert to previous image tag, escalate to CI/build to produce reproducible image.

3) Symptom: terraform apply stuck on resource replacement for hours and then times out.
   - Hypothesis: network ACL blocking cloud provider API callbacks or remote state backend.
   - Probes: tcpdump on control-plane outbound to state backend; check provider error messages in plan; verify IAM creds not expired.
   - Mitigation: abort apply, terraform apply -target to isolate, or restore from saved tfstate and rerun.

4) Symptom: model outputs garbled or tokenization errors after upgrade.
   - Hypothesis: tokenizer data mismatch between model artifact and runtime; KV cache schema changed with new runtime.
   - Probes: run a tokenization test harness, compare hashes of tokenizer files in /opt/models.
   - Mitigation: fallback to previous model artifact, enable compatibility layer, and run migration tooling.

5) Symptom: image pulls failing intermittently with 403/401 from artifact registry.
   - Hypothesis: expiring short-lived tokens, or IP egress changed and registry ACLs block new IPs.
   - Probes: curl token endpoint, check registry audit logs, verify NAT IPs.
   - Mitigation: refresh credentials, coordinate with network team to update ACLs, re-run pulls.

Quick log snippets we look for (examples):
- GPU reset: "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:01:00): 79"
- NVML busy/hung: "Failed to initialize NVML: Unknown Error"
- Containerd OOM: "oom_kill: Killed process"
- Kernel module load fail: "modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'nvidia': Unknown symbol in module"

Packaging the smoke result (minimal reproducible artifact):
- compressed bundle containing: tf-plan.txt, /tmp/state.json, kubectl get pods -n redwood -o yaml, logs (last 200 lines) for 3 runtime pods, dmesg snippet, nvidia-smi output. Name as redwood-smoke-<cluster>-YYYYMMDD.tar.gz.

Known flaky resources & mitigations:
- NFS mounts for model storage: add retry wrapper and mount options (noac, soft) in tf module.
- Local docker registry certificates: include an init probe to fail early if CA not present.
- Host kernel auto-upgrades: disable automatic kernel updates or coordinate maintenance windows.

ToDos / open questions:
- Add an automated drift detector that runs nightly and posts tfstate diffs to a channel.
- Improve canary traffic generator to include long-context traces (we only use short prompts today).
- Decide on a standard timeout policy for terraform applies in customer environments (30m vs 2h).

Escalation contacts (who to ping):
- eng-private-deployments on-call: #eng-private-deployments (Slack)
- Maya Patel (owner) - maya@redwood.ai
- Diego Morales (SRE lead) - diego@redwood.ai
- Infra on-call escalation (pager duty): PD: infra-cust

Postmortem template (copy into incident doc):
- Incident ID, timeline, what changed, smoke-harness outputs, root cause hypothesis, corrective actions, followups assigned.

Notes to self: Keep this doc short and pragmatic. If a pattern recurs 3x for different customers, spin out a dedicated runbook with automated probes and remediation scripts.
